blocks.text: HANGS Construction Services LLC. Invented procedures for a software demonstration.

Actuals are the closed general ledger by department. Contract revenue is 4100 with the over/under billing adjustment in 4150; contract costs are 5100 with the loss provision in 5150. The year to date runs from July 1, the start of the fiscal year.

The budget is the board-approved FY2027 operating budget by department, account and month, with contract revenue budgeted by job at each job's bid margin. It is not changed after approval; the reforecast is shown beside it.

A variance needs a written explanation when it is more than 5% of budget and more than $10,000, for the month or the year to date, on any department line and on any job's revenue or gross profit. Favorable and unfavorable variances are treated alike.

Contract costs, fuel and small tools vary with contract revenue. The flex budget restates them at actual revenue: each job's contract cost at its budgeted cost ratio, fuel at 1.10% and small tools at 0.60% of contract revenue. Budget to flex budget is the volume variance; flex budget to actual is the margin or spending variance.

Each line owner explains the cause in plain English, says whether it is timing or permanent, and gives its effect on the rest of the year. Finance tests every explanation against the general ledger lines; an explanation the ledger does not support goes back to its owner and the commentary states what the ledger shows.

The reforecast is the actual year to date plus the rest of the year: backlog on signed contracts as the project managers schedule it at each job's current estimate, new work only under a signed contract, overhead at budget adjusted for the known changes in the reforecast inputs, and variable costs at the budget rates. Work without a signed contract is shown separately as upside and is not in the reforecast.

A posting error found in the review, such as a prepayment expensed when paid, is proposed as a correcting entry for the Controller, and the report shows the corrected figure beside the booked one. An outlay over $5,000 that extends an asset's life is raised with the Controller as a possible capital item.

The board pack is one page: contract revenue, gross profit, overhead and net income for the month and the year to date against budget, the variances over the threshold with their explanations, and the reforecast against the full-year budget. The CFO reviews and signs it before release. The preparer posts nothing and sends nothing.

sheets.name: Notes
rows: Revenue is under budget for three reasons. Larch Hollow Building 3 hit rock at the driveway cut: the excavation and a retaining wall were not in the bid, so the estimate went up and the job's percent complete, and with it earned revenue, went down; the whole loss is booked. Ridgecrest's revenue is held until its project manager updates the estimate. And the new work we budgeted to start in October has not been awarded yet. On the other side, Bellhaven is earning more than its bid margin now that the signed CO-03 controls work is in the contract.
Costs are under budget because volume is under budget. On a like-for-like basis Larch Hollow Building 3 is well over, for the site work above.
Fuel and repair costs ran higher with the heavier site work schedule in October.
We renewed the estimating and takeoff software on the annual plan in October; the annual plan is cheaper per month than the monthly plan it replaces.
Counsel reviewed our lien rights and the collections letter on the Orchard Gate clubhouse (S-2598), which is past 90 days. One-time; a smaller follow-up is expected in November and December.

policies.title: Actuals
policies.text: Actuals are the closed general ledger by department. Contract revenue is 4100 with the over/under billing adjustment in 4150; contract costs are 5100 with the loss provision in 5150. The year to date runs from July 1, the start of the fiscal year.
policies.source: HANGS Budget and Variance Policy v2.0.docx

policies.title: The Budget
policies.text: The budget is the board-approved FY2027 operating budget by department, account and month, with contract revenue budgeted by job at each job's bid margin. It is not changed after approval; the reforecast is shown beside it.
policies.source: HANGS Budget and Variance Policy v2.0.docx

policies.title: Variance Thresholds
policies.text: A variance needs a written explanation when it is more than 5% of budget and more than $10,000, for the month or the year to date, on any department line and on any job's revenue or gross profit. Favorable and unfavorable variances are treated alike.
policies.source: HANGS Budget and Variance Policy v2.0.docx

policies.title: Flex Budget
policies.text: Contract costs, fuel and small tools vary with contract revenue. The flex budget restates them at actual revenue: each job's contract cost at its budgeted cost ratio, fuel at 1.10% and small tools at 0.60% of contract revenue. Budget to flex budget is the volume variance; flex budget to actual is the margin or spending variance.
policies.source: HANGS Budget and Variance Policy v2.0.docx

policies.title: Explanations
policies.text: Each line owner explains the cause in plain English, says whether it is timing or permanent, and gives its effect on the rest of the year. Finance tests every explanation against the general ledger lines; an explanation the ledger does not support goes back to its owner and the commentary states what the ledger shows.
policies.source: HANGS Budget and Variance Policy v2.0.docx

policies.title: Reforecast
policies.text: The reforecast is the actual year to date plus the rest of the year: backlog on signed contracts as the project managers schedule it at each job's current estimate, new work only under a signed contract, overhead at budget adjusted for the known changes in the reforecast inputs, and variable costs at the budget rates. Work without a signed contract is shown separately as upside and is not in the reforecast.
policies.source: HANGS Budget and Variance Policy v2.0.docx

policies.title: Corrections
policies.text: A posting error found in the review, such as a prepayment expensed when paid, is proposed as a correcting entry for the Controller, and the report shows the corrected figure beside the booked one. An outlay over $5,000 that extends an asset's life is raised with the Controller as a possible capital item.
policies.source: HANGS Budget and Variance Policy v2.0.docx

policies.title: Board Pack and Review
policies.text: The board pack is one page: contract revenue, gross profit, overhead and net income for the month and the year to date against budget, the variances over the threshold with their explanations, and the reforecast against the full-year budget. The CFO reviews and signs it before release. The preparer posts nothing and sends nothing.
policies.source: HANGS Budget and Variance Policy v2.0.docx

checks.title: Annual Plan Expensed When Paid · BVA-7, BVA-5
checks.detail: Tallyset Software invoice TS-44817, $16,800.00 for November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027, was expensed in October. PRE software is $17,600.00 for October against a $800.00 budget. The chief estimator's note is right that the plan was renewed, but the whole $16,800.00 covers November 2026 to October 2027: none of it is an October cost. Under BVA-7, RC-01 moves it to 1350 Prepaid Expenses; from November it is expensed at $1,400.00 a month. Corrected, October software is $800.00, on budget, and October's net loss is $16,800.00 smaller. The reforecast carries the annual plan at $1,400.00 a month, $600.00 over the budget's $800.00.

checks.title: Explanation Not Supported · BVA-5, BVA-7
checks.detail: FLD equipment repairs are $12,060.00 over budget; the note blames fuel and a heavier schedule, the ledger shows one $11,850.00 pump rebuild. October repairs are $13,660.00 against $1,600.00. The equipment manager's note says fuel and repair costs ran higher with a heavier site schedule. The ledger does not support it: fuel was $1,984.85 under budget for October; contract volume was 42.2% under budget. One line is 98% of the variance: Tamarack Equipment Service invoice 2291, excavator hydraulic pump rebuild, unit EX-04, $11,850.00. Without it, repairs were $1,810.00, $210.00 over budget. Under BVA-5 the note goes back to its owner and the commentary says what the ledger shows. Under BVA-7 the rebuild is over $5,000.00 and the invoice says it extends the unit's life by about three years, so it is raised with the Controller as a possible capital item; no entry is proposed until the Controller decides.

checks.title: Unsigned Award in the Reforecast · BVA-6
checks.detail: Alder Crossing Medical Office Tenant Improvement, $640,000.00, is in the submitted reforecast without a signed contract. The business development manager's reforecast carries Alder Crossing Medical Office Tenant Improvement for Alder Crossing Medical Group LLC at $640,000.00 of revenue from January to May, status “Verbal award; contract not signed”. BVA-6 admits new work only under a signed contract, so this reforecast leaves it out and shows it as upside: $640,000.00 of revenue and $73,600.00 of gross profit at its 11.5% estimated margin. With it, full-year revenue would be $3,105,050.23 instead of $2,465,050.23. Halvorsen Dental Lab Fit-Out ($412,000.00), signed October 28, 2026, is in. If the contract is signed before the board meets, the CFO can move it into the reforecast.

checks.title: Revenue Held on an Unrevised Estimate · BVA-5, BVA-6
checks.detail: Ridgecrest Veterinary Exam Room Expansion (S-2607) earned nothing in October against $38,000.00 budgeted; its estimate was last revised September 22, 2026. The approved WIP schedule holds S-2607's earned revenue at September's level because its project manager did not revise the estimate to complete for October, while $21,350.00 of October cost went in. So October shows a $21,350.00 gross loss on the job, and its $38,000.00 revenue shortfall is timing, not lost work, until the estimate is revised. The reforecast uses the same unrevised estimate: $81,397.89 of backlog at a $72,000.00 cost to complete, $9,397.89 of gross profit for the rest of the year. The CFO should not sign the job's numbers as final until the project manager dates a new estimate (WIP-4).
